  Exam Date & Time: 15-Nov-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Pattern classification [IT_5006]  
  Marks: 50                                                                                  Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           A university plans to replace traditional ID cards with a biometric-based attendance  
  system that uses both facial recognition and fingerprint verification. During  
  implementation, the system faces challenges in recognizing students under varying  
  A)      lighting conditions and partial fingerprint captures.  
  Illustrate the challenges this system faces from the perspective of pattern recognition       (5)  
  design. Explain how feature extraction, classification, and decision-making steps play a  
  role here. Also, classify the type of pattern recognition method (statistical, structural, or  
  syntactic) primarily used and justify your answer  
  
  B)      A retail company collects large amounts of purchase history and demographic data from  
  its customers but lacks labeled data. The company aims to group customers with similar  
  shopping behaviors to design targeted marketing strategies.  
  
  Describe how unsupervised learning techniques can be applied in this scenario. Explain (5)  
  the concept of feature space and how clusters represent implicit classes. Discuss how the  
  resulting decision boundaries differ from those in supervised learning and the challenges  
  involved in evaluating cluster quality.  
  
  2)           An AI company is building two products:  
  
  • Product A: Automatically reads and digitizes handwritten documents.  
  A)          • Product B: Converts spoken language into text commands for smart assistants.  
  
  Both systems rely on pattern recognition but process different types of data (visual and  
  auditory).                                                                                        (5)  
  
  Compare and contrast the pattern recognition processes in Product A and Product B.  
  Discuss how data representation, feature selection, and classification techniques differ  
  between the two. Further, identify the type of pattern (statistical, structural, or syntactic)  
  each system most likely employs and justify with appropriate examples.  
  
  B)      A team of researchers is developing an autonomous drone navigation system that learns (5)  
  optimal flight paths through trial and error. The drone receives rewards for efficient  
  routes and penalties for collisions or deviations from the target zone.  
  
  Analyze how reinforcement learning serves as a paradigm of pattern recognition in this

  scenario. Explain how the drone's state, action, and reward can be represented in feature  
  space, and discuss how decision boundaries evolve dynamically as learning progresses.  
  Compare this paradigm with supervised and unsupervised learning in terms of feedback  
  and data requirements.  
  
  3)        A human-computer interaction (HCI) team is developing a gesture recognition system to  
  classify hand movements into actions like swipe left, swipe right, zoom in, and zoom  
  out.  
  A)   Analyze how the distance metric selection (e.g., Euclidean vs. Manhattan) influences the (5)  
  classifier's sensitivity to noisy sensor data.  
  Compare the effectiveness of 1-NN, k-NN, and weighted k-NN in handling ambiguous  
  gestures.  
  
  B)   A computer vision team is building an image classification model to identify plant  
  species from leaf images. Initially, the training dataset contains over 50,000 labeled  
  samples, leading to high computation time in the k-Nearest Neighbor classifier. To  
  reduce processing time without losing accuracy, the team applies prototype selection  
  techniques such as Condensed Nearest Neighbour (CNN) and Edited Nearest Neighbour  
  (ENN).                                                                                 (5)  
  
  Explain how CNN and ENN algorithms can be applied to optimize the training set in  
  this scenario. Compare their working principles, objectives, and effects on classification  
  accuracy and computational efficiency. Illustrate how each method modifies the  
  prototype set and why such reduction is beneficial.  
  
  4)        A hospital's AI department is developing a diagnostic system that classifies patients as  
  either disease-positive or disease-negative based on test results (e.g., blood sugar,  
  cholesterol, BMI). Each class has known prior probabilities and likelihoods estimated  
  A)   from historical data.  
  
  Illustrate how a Bayes classifier can be used to make optimal decisions in this medical (5)  
  diagnosis scenario. Using the concept of minimum error rate classification, explain how  
  the decision boundary between the two classes is determined. Discuss how changing  
  prior probabilities (e.g., due to prevalence of disease) affects the classification outcome  
  and error rate.  
  
  B)   A financial institution uses customer data (income, credit history, debt ratio,  
  employment type) to classify applicants as low-risk or high-risk for loan approval. The  
  data contains overlapping cases where some high-risk customers have similar profiles to  
  low-risk ones, making perfect separation impossible.  
  (5)  
  Analyze how an SVM classifier with slack variables can handle this real-world dataset  
  where classes are not perfectly separable. Explain the trade-off between margin width  
  and classification error, and how the regularization parameter (C) influences this  
  balance.  
  
  5)        A tech company is developing an automated document recognition system that converts (5)  
  scanned documents into editable text using Optical Character Recognition (OCR). To  
  improve recognition accuracy across different fonts and languages, the developers  
  A)   combine multiple classifiers using bagging, boosting, and stacking techniques.  
  
  Analyze how ensemble learning methods (bagging, boosting, and stacking) can improve

  the performance of OCR systems in this scenario. Explain the working principles of  
  each technique and how they address errors from individual classifiers. Discuss the  
  trade-offs between computational complexity and accuracy when combining multiple  
  classifiers in document recognition tasks  
  
  B)            A digital library project aims to organize scanned research papers into categories (e.g.,  
  computer science, biology, economics). Each document contains a mix of text blocks,  
  figures, tables, and equations. The team decides to use feature extraction techniques to  
  represent the visual and textual structure of documents before classification.  
  Explain how feature extraction in document processing can be used to classify  
  documents in this scenario. Identify the types of features (e.g., text density, font size, (5)  
  object layout, keyword frequency) that could help in distinguishing document  
  categories. Discuss how extracted features can be represented numerically and how they  
  contribute to pattern recognition or machine learning models for document  
  classification.
